transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I'm here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it really should. Just the idea of getting on a plane makes me... I just picture that really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight all over again. I mean, I know people fly safely every single day, but I just can't seem to shake it.
Aside from when you're thinking about or planning a flight, do you ever have unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that turbulence experience popping up on their own?

No, not really. Um, it doesn't just pop up out of nowhere. I don't have nightmares about it or flashbacks or anything like that. 

It's really just... if I have to book a ticket or if I know a trip is coming up, that's when I start picturing it and get all worked up. But on a normal day at work or whatever, no, it doesn't cross my mind.
Aside from flying, do you notice similar intense fear or a strong urge to avoid other situations, like being in enclosed spaces or at heights?
No, not really. Um, I don't have any issues with heights or small spaces or anything like that. I take the elevator every day at work and it doesn't bother me at all. It really is just the flying.
When you're actually at the airport or on the plane, do you experience an immediate rush of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's actually not even just at the airport. Like, if I'm looking at flights for an upcoming conference, or honestly, even if I just hear a plane flying overhead, my chest tightens up right away. I get this sudden rush of panic, and I just feel like I need to shut my laptop or get away from the thought entirely. It's pretty immediate.
How long has this fear of flying been going on—was it right after your honeymoon flight, or did it start more recently?
Yeah, it was right after. It's been going on ever since that turbulent flight back from my honeymoon. So, um, that would be about two years and five months ago now.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a marked, persistent, and excessive fear of flying that began immediately after a specific frightening turbulence event ~2.5 years ago. Fear is cued specifically by flying-related stimuli (booking tickets, seeing planes, planning trips) and produces immediate physiological anxiety response (chest tightness, panic) with strong urge to avoid. The fear is circumscribed to flying only—no fear of heights, enclosed spaces, or other situations. Importantly, there are no intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares occurring spontaneously outside of flying-related triggers, which argues against PTSD despite the traumatic origin of the fear. The clinical picture is best characterized as a specific (situational) phobia rather than a generalized anxiety disorder or PTSD.
